## Introduction

The broadcast to the studios can be established in different ways:

1.  **Digital audio via Internet**
    -   SIP call (full-duplex with minimal latency).
    -   RTP streaming (transmission only).
    -   Shoutcast/Icecast server.
2.  **Mobile phone call** (Bluetooth).
3.  **Land line phone call** (POTS).

In practice, once the Internet broadcast options are configured, the user only needs to **connect the MX2200 to the Internet** and start the desired transmission, without requiring additional configurations.

The broadcast methods can be combined, either to have a **backup** (e.g., SIP + mobile phone) or as a **complement** (RTP streaming + private telephone communication with the studio).

---

sections.translation: ## Internet Connection The CODEC-MIXER MX2200 can connect to the Internet in three ways. Only **one connection** can be active at a time, although it is possible to configure more than one so that if one fails, the console re-establishes the connection automatically via another route. Connect the Wi-Fi antenna (provided) to a rear USB port labeled **Wi-Fi**. If it already recognizes a previously used network and the credentials are still valid, the connection will be automatic, making the following steps unnecessary. The Wi-Fi icon will appear at the top of the HOME screen. Initially it will be displayed in gray (no signal). Turn the encoder to **SETUP**, press to access, and then select **Wi-Fi**.\ A list of available networks will be displayed. Choose the desired network and enter the password using the **DATA ENTRY** keyboard. - If the password is valid, the network assigns an IP address (visible in **SETUP/Wi-Fi**). This may take a few seconds. - If it is incorrect, the IP will remain **0.0.0.0** and you must repeat the procedure. Once connected, the Wi-Fi icon on the main screen will show the **signal strength**.\ The unit is ready for SIP calls, RTP streaming, or web server connection. You can check Internet access by connecting a mobile phone or notebook to the same Wi-Fi network and browsing the web.\ It is also possible to use a **mobile phone in Hotspot mode**, creating a Wi-Fi node to which the MX2200 will connect. **Open public networks**\ Always verify the network being used. On open networks with a web login, the MX2200 may indicate "connection OK" even if there is no real Internet access. Using a standard UTP cable, connect the MX2200's **Ethernet** port to the local network. From the factory, the console has **DHCP enabled**, so the router/switch will automatically assign an IP address. On the **SETUP** screen, confirm that a valid address (different from **0.0.0.0**) has been assigned. To check Internet access, connect a notebook to the same network and open a web browser. Connect a **4G/5G USB modem** (not provided) to the indicated rear ports.\ Use a USB extension cable of at least **30 cm**. Once detected, the **4G** icon will be displayed on the main screen. The unit is ready to initiate SIP calls, RTP streaming, or web server connection. Do not connect the modem **directly** to the console: it can cause **audio interference**.\ Always use the USB extension cable.
